newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian railmen on strike over pay, conditions.
newsitem.headline: Croatian railmen on strike over pay, conditions.

text.p: Croatian rail workers launched a new strike on Saturday for higher wages and improved working conditions, but gave passenger trains a reprieve until after the New Year holidays, state news agency HINA said.
Their union halted all cargo trains except those protected by law against strike action, believed to include trains serving the military and the NATO-led peacekeeping force in Bosnia.
But passenger trains would be allowed to run until January 2, when the union would probably introduce only a skeleton service, the agency said.
The loss-making state railways (HZ) said on Saturday it had failed to reach any agreement with the union as it was "unable to meet their demands", HINA said.
The railmen called off a previous three-week strike on December 17 after the Supreme Court upheld its own ruling that the stoppage by 11,000 workers was illegal.
HZ has said it was planning to sue the union for losses caused by the stoppage totalling 20 million kuna ($3.6 million).
The government has refused to give in to workers' demands, saying there was no money to increase pay this year.
The HZ is getting more than one billion kuna ($200 million) under the 1996 budget, but the government has said it wants to keep the subsidy below that level next year.
